claims.explanation: Didanosine is a nucleoside analog that, after intracellular phosphorylation, inhibits mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma and also requires purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) for activation; selectivity likely reflects dependence on purine salvage/PNP-mediated activation and on mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma, so lines with high PNP expression or low mitochondrial reserve are more sensitive. The pattern of sensitive lines is enriched for RAS/RTK-MAPK pathway activation (KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, ALK, NF1 loss), which may increase nucleotide demand and dependence on salvage pathways, while protective lines often retain wild-type-like PNP pathway or have intact DNA repair/checkpoint features.

features.basis: PNP is the annotated didanosine target and activates purine nucleoside analogs; high expression should increase drug activation
KRAS-mutant lines (SW480, LU99, NCIH1792, GP2D) are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with increased nucleotide salvage demand
BRAF-mutant lines (AM38, CAL12T, RPMI7951, RL952) appear among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven nucleotide dependence
NRAS-mutant HEPG2 is sensitive, and RAS pathway activation may increase dependence on purine salvage
HRAS-mutant RL952 is sensitive, supporting RAS pathway activation as a sensitizing context
EGFR-mutant lines (NCIH1650, RL952, KYSE70) are sensitive, consistent with RTK-driven nucleotide demand
ERBB2-mutant SW480 is sensitive, suggesting ERBB-driven proliferation increases sensitivity
ALK-mutant NCIH2452 is sensitive, consistent with oncogenic RTK signaling increasing purine demand
NF1-mutant lines (COLO792, GP2D) are sensitive, consistent with RAS pathway activation
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, but many least-affected lines are TP53-mutant, suggesting it is not sufficient and may correlate with resistance in this context
CDKN2A loss appears frequently in least-affected lines (MHHES1, RD, BHY, VMCUB1, KELLY), suggesting intact CDK4/6-RB checkpoint may be needed for didanosine sensitivity
PTEN mutation appears in several least-affected lines (8MGBA, SF295, OVK18), suggesting PI3K-AKT activation may reduce dependence on purine salvage
